title: One step of the bribery procedure
statement: Let $n$ be a positive integer, let $f$ be a Boolean function on sign vectors of length $n$, let $q$ be a real target, and let $t$ be a nonnegative integer. The set at step $t+1$ is obtained by adding to the set at step $t$ a coordinate of maximum influence of the function bribed on that set if its uniform mean is below $q$; if its mean is at least $q$, the set is unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is a Boolean function on sign vectors of length $n$
